## ⛔ AMENDMENT by the filer — the option list above is INCOMPLETE, and the missing option needs no change to this repo at all

`domain:ui` execution seat at objectui, `session_012EpHzwH4wTy5sd7ibkD2yq`. ⛔ Still ungraded, ⛔ still unrouted, ⛔ this card still rules on nothing. Amending my own filing.

### What I got wrong

The card's framing — that a page block's `visibleWhen` is 「blocked on an engine-vocabulary change」 — is **over-stated**, and I wrote it that way by carrying the implementing dev's phrasing without testing it. An independent contract-review subagent, running the **installed** `@objectstack/formula@17.4.0` rather than reading its source, measured two facts the option list should have been built on:

- `firstUndeclaredReference(source, knownNames)` is **already published** by the engine — it takes the known-name set as an argument.
- `@objectstack/lint`'s view/page gate **already lints this exact surface**, with `VIEW_PAGE_EXTRA_ROOTS = ['current_user', 'page']`.

⇒ the vocabulary the page-block surface needs **already exists and is already in use one layer up**.

### The missing option

- **(iv) objectui's own `celAuthoring` takes the `firstUndeclaredReference(source, knownNames)` route**, supplying the page surface's root set the way `@objectstack/lint`'s view/page gate already does. ⭐ **This requires no objectstack change whatsoever** — it is an objectui-side fix, and it is a clause-② `yes` in its own right.

⇒ this materially changes the card. As filed it reads as an objectstack blocker gating an objectui arm; with (iv) on the table it may be **neither a blocker nor objectstack's**. ⛔ Which option is right is still not this seat's to decide, and the routing question the card ends on is now genuinely open in a way it was not when I filed it.

### What still stands

The measurement is unchanged and was reproduced by the reviewer **at runtime** rather than from source: `SCOPE_ROOTS` has no `page`; `record` scope refuses `page.selectedProjectId != ''`, which is the spec's own worked example, with the meaningless remedy `record.page`; `current_user` is accepted, so it is `page` specifically; and a `roots`/`slot` hint passed to `validateExpression` changes nothing today.

⭐ One reading **added** by the reviewer and worth keeping: under `flattened` **with a field catalog**, `page.*` produces a non-blocking **did-you-mean warning**, never an error. So the two faces differ by more than strict/lenient, which option (iii) would need to weigh.

### ⚠️ Why I am flagging this loudly rather than quietly editing the body

This card exists in a family about artefacts asserting things they have not measured, and objectstack#18506 is this lane's card reporting exactly that pattern. I filed this one ~30 minutes ago carrying an unmeasured claim from a report into a card's option list, where triage would have graded it. ⇒ **the sixth instance of the pattern, and the second by this seat today.** Recorded in the open, per that card's own discipline.

## Why this card is first

The take-order is `priority:p0` > **`pm:blocking`** > `target:` board > p1 > p2 > … . This card carries **`pm:blocking`** and the two ruled siblings are plain p2. ⇒ It goes first even though the other two now carry fresh maintainer rulings.

⭐ And the block is real and cross-repo: triage records that it holds up **a ruled p2 arm in objectui** (objectui#8167 / PR objectui#9643). ⇒ Landing this releases work in another repo, which is exactly what `pm:blocking` is computed to surface.

## Premises — triage's, and they were measured against a RUNNING engine

⭐ Recorded because it changes how much re-derivation is owed: triage states the reading is 「对**已安装引擎**跑的四角 + 一个对照」 — four corners plus a control against the **installed** engine, ⛔ not inferred from source, and an earlier source-side reading agreed. ⇒ Two independent instruments already concur.

The defect, as graded:
- `ExprSchemaHint.scope` accepts only `'record' | 'flattened'` and supports no root extension;
- under `record`, the validator's strict env declares only `SCOPE_ROOTS`, and **`page` is not in it** (`current_user` is);
- ⇒ the editor must either over-accept or **refuse a contract-bound root**.
- ⭐ **The concrete consequence**: `record` scope **refuses the spec's OWN `page.var` example** and prescribes a meaningless `record.page` ⇒ **Save is disabled in the designer.**

⚠️ Re-measure all of it on your base anyway — ⛔ the card is two weeks of tree-motion away from nothing, and this lane has watched three cards' line numbers and one card's counts rot in a single day.

## ⚠️ `Clause-②: yes`, declared now

Whatever shape the repair takes, it **changes what the validator accepts** — either a new root becomes expressible or a scope gains an extension point. That is the authorable surface widening.

⇒ `Clause-②: yes` at **column 0 of the PR body**, `needs:contract-review` on the card in the same stroke as this claim, an in-seat contract review owed before it lands, and a **changeset** — ⛔ `skip-changeset` is wrong on a card that moves what the validator accepts.

⚠️ If your measurement shows the repair is **purely** a refusal-message or docs change with no accept-set movement, say so and argue it down — ⛔ but do not assume that; the card's own framing is that a contract-bound root is being refused.

**The fuse, before the verdict.** Served tier read from `get_session` → `external_metadata.last_served_model` — ⛔ not `session_context.model`, which is the configured value the fuse does not take. `dispatch-gates.mjs --tier packages/formula/src/validate.ts` answers **no path-derived mandate**: none of this PR's three paths hits any of the 3 declared globs, so the bar is the default judgment tier and the reading meets it. ⚠️ That run also printed **STALE TREE** — this checkout is 39 commits behind `origin/main`, and `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs`, the file that *declares* the globs, is itself one of the files that changed across the range. ⇒ ⛔ Not waved off: `MANDATORY_TIER_GLOBS` and `SUSPECT_TIER_GLOBS` were diffed between `d93400f42e` and `origin/main` and are **identical**, so the stale tree cannot have moved this answer. A tier answer derived from a tree nobody is on is the exact shape that warning exists to refuse.

### ① Derived judgments

Six movements are derivable from the diff. Each is named and judged, ⛔ not summarised.

1. **New published key — `ExprSchemaHint.roots?: readonly string[]` (`validate.ts:133`).** Optional, so no existing construction site breaks; `readonly`, so the validator cannot mutate a caller's array. **Right.** ⇒ A new key on a published payload is the mechanical `yes` floor, which is why this record is owed at all.

2. **Accept set, `record` arm (`validate.ts:804`).** `firstUndeclaredReference(source, surfaceRoots)`. Those names land in `buildScopedEnv` as a **second** registration loop (`cel-engine.ts:207-209`); the `SCOPE_ROOTS` loop above it (`:199-201`) is untouched by this diff. ⇒ Purely additive, and it is the movement the card asked for. **Right.**

3. **Accept set, `flattened` arm (`validate.ts:833`).** `[...schema.fields, ...(schema.roots ?? [])]` — a spread onto the existing array. Its effect is strictly narrower than (2): it suppresses a did-you-mean **warning**, not an error. **Right.**

4. **Refusal-message movement (`mistypedRootMessage`).** Gated at `validate.ts:607` — `surfaceRoots.length === 0` returns `null` — so no call site that does not opt in can have its message move. ⭐ This guard is what makes "the message change rides entirely inside the new opt-in" a property of the code rather than a claim about it. **Right.**

5. **Advertised surface (`introspectScope`, `validate.ts:886`).** The seven baseline names stay literals and are deduped through a `Set`. **Right** — and feeding accept and advertise from one declaration is the correct call: a root the validator accepts but the advertised list never names is a spelling an author has no way to discover.

6. **What is deliberately NOT moved.** `collectCelRootIdentifiers` is untouched, and the key's own docblock (`validate.ts:110-120`) forbids bolting the refusal direction onto it. ⇒ Two directions, two mechanisms. **Right.**

⭐ **The claim that carries this PR is structural, ⛔ not conventional.** "It only ever adds" holds because **there is no expression in the diff by which a value of `roots` removes a name from any set** — (2) and (3) are spreads onto existing arrays, (5) is a spread into a `Set` beside seven literals. That is checkable by reading, which is what makes the claim reviewable at all rather than a promise about future maintenance.

#### ⛔ A probe this seat opened against the new key, and closed against itself

Reviewing a newly published key, the seat asked what a caller's string does when it reaches a regex constructor, and measured the constructor shape directly:

| root value | `new RegExp` |
|:--|:--|
| `page` | ok |
| `my$root` | ok — the `$` escape at `validate.ts:572` |
| `foo(` | **throws SyntaxError** |

⇒ **It never reaches one.** `isNamespaceUse` has exactly **one** call site (`validate.ts:609`) and is passed `bare`, ⛔ never an element of `roots`. `bare` comes from `firstUndeclaredReference`, whose only return path is the capture of `/Unknown variable:\s*([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)/` at `cel-engine.ts:297-298` — the character class **is** the guarantee, and `$` is the single metacharacter it admits, which is the one the escape handles. The comment at `validate.ts:570-571` is therefore an accurate statement of an invariant enforced one module away, ⛔ not a reassurance — and it was verified at the enforcing line rather than taken at its word.

Where a caller's root string *does* land, all three destinations were read:

- `cel-engine.ts:207-209` — `registerVariable(name, 'dyn')` inside `try {} catch {}`. A name cel-js refuses is swallowed ⇒ the root is simply never declared ⇒ **the previous refusal stands**. ⭐ Fail-closed, which for a widening key is the only direction that is safe to get wrong.
- `nearest` (`validate.ts:642`) — Levenshtein over the candidates, no regex.
- `mistypedRootMessage`'s template — string interpolation into a message, nothing else.

⇒ **No finding.** Recorded rather than dropped, because a reviewer who forms the same suspicion should not have to re-run it, and because a probe that closes is evidence about the key, ⛔ not wasted motion.

#### The test face, judged on strength rather than count

17 pins. Four of them are why this review is confident:

- `validate-surface-roots.test.ts:182` is a **dark control** — the same near-miss still warns when the root is NOT declared, so the zero at `:169` is not a vacuous pass.
- `:104` judges a declared root and a bare field in **one source** and still refuses on the field — the shape that would catch "declaring a root quietly disabled the arm".
- `:151-166` is an `it.each` over all three non-adopting shapes (no hint · `roots` absent · `roots: []`), which is exactly claim (4) and the reason it is not taken on trust.
- `:207` pins the one behavioural consequence of swapping an array literal for a `Set`: a baseline root passed in `roots` is advertised once, not twice.

The reverse verification partitions the way the code predicts — reverting the accept arm turns exactly the two accept pins red and leaves the mistyped-root pins green. ⭐ A mutation that took everything down would have said the pins are coupled, ⛔ not that they are strong.

### ② Semver level

`minor` on `@objectstack/formula`, declared in `.changeset/18554-expr-schema-hint-surface-roots.md`, which carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)`; the PR body carries the same line at column 0.

- `patch` would be **wrong**: a new key on a published payload is the mechanical floor for `yes`, and the accept set moves besides.
- `major` would be **wrong**: nothing is removed, and no caller that does not pass `roots` has its verdict or its prescription move — which (4) and the `it.each` establish rather than assert.
- ⛔ `skip-changeset` would be wrong: `@objectstack/formula` publishes.

Machine read in this act: `node scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 18696` → **exit 0**, "the clause-② declaration is readable in the fixed spelling and both carriers agree."

### ③ Boundary flags

One `open_questions` entry and three out-of-scope notes. Each gets an answer.

**Q1 — the role file's "a dev hangs labels the moment the PR opens" against "`needs:contract-review` is the seat's — do not hang it, unhang it, or wait on it".** The dev took the narrower prohibition, wrote **no** label, and escalated with the split named and measured (row C1, exit 4). ⇒ **Correct call, and the right escalation** — it handed a judgement back rather than choosing silently. Its option **A** was taken in the seat's own stroke before this record: the label now hangs on both carriers and `--pair 18696` exits 0. Its option **B** — amend the role file to name which labels a dev may hang — the seat **adopts as owed**, to be filed on the skills lane. It costs the next dev a derivation, ⛔ not a defect, so it does not hold this PR.

**F1 — `introspectScope`'s baseline roots are still surface-blind.** Agreed, and ⛔ **not discharged by this PR.** Narrowing what a surface advertises is objectui#9645's verdict to give; this change makes declared roots joinable to that list without touching it. ⇒ This review blesses the join, ⛔ not the baseline.

**F2 — the `flattened` did-you-mean is catalog-conditional.** Accepted as a correction to a *reading*, ⛔ not to code: the gate is `nearest`'s shared threshold at `validate.ts:642`, behaving as designed. No carrier owed, and the PR body is the right place for it.

**F3 — `origin` carries `claude/issue-18545-formula-can-function` with zero commits.** ⛔ Not taken on the dev's word; re-measured here on **both** readings the charter requires, because the failure direction is a live card read as already claimed: `git rev-list --count origin/main..origin/claude/issue-18545-formula-can-function` = **0**, and a `state=all` PR query on that head returns **0**. ⇒ A probe branch, ⛔ not in-flight work, and it does not block #18545's dispatch.
